eras.label: Three fixes, the edge court, wider ranges

log.title: The midnight hour stays with yesterday
log.what: IEM's daily maximum is for the calendar day on daylight time, so for the first hour after midnight it holds a reading from the previous climate day. It is no longer used as a floor when only a reading from before the climate day started could have produced it.
log.why: At 12:56 AM on 10-02 New York's floor was 72, the 12:51 AM reading from 10-01's climate day. Harmless that night; on a day warmest at midnight it would sit above the real high all day.

log.title: Two evening-pick fixes
log.what: The airport's five-minute maximum, which is in whole degrees Celsius, no longer overrides the six-hour maximum once the day is decided. A climate-report figure is taken as the day's high only if every hourly reading after its as-of time is at least a degree under it.
log.why: Austin read 99 to 100 from 7 PM on four days that settled 98. New York's 6 PM final said 72 to 73 at 100% on a day that settled 74. Replayed on the September trail: 332 evening rows moved to the settled bracket, 21 moved off it (one Austin evening).

log.title: The floor is what was measured
log.what: The ladder used to delete every outcome below the hourly maximum plus its average gap to the true peak. That gap is an average, so on a day whose hourly reading was the peak it deleted the range that settles. The cut is now the readings themselves; the estimate still sets the centre. A five-minute reading counts as the latest only when it is newer than the hourly report.
log.why: Las Vegas held 94 to 95 at 87% all evening on 09-30 against a market at 99.5% on 92 to 93. Replayed on the September trail, log loss fell from 0.91 to 0.81 across the three cities (Las Vegas 0.86 to 0.65), picks level.

log.title: Three fixes, the edge court, wider ranges
log.what: A peak-wind remark is no longer read as a temperature. A six-hour minimum more than 3 degrees under every hourly reading is not believed. The evening pick takes the printed climate report over an estimate. A bet is named only where a market's own graded bets have earned one. The spread answers to the live locks: New York and Austin widened to 1.25, Las Vegas kept at 0.75.
log.why: A week of 8 right in 18 on the highs. The bets named since launch had won 39% where the sheet said 72%, and the market's odds beat ours at every hour.

log.title: Morning-wind correction, wired in and left off
log.what: A lean by morning wind direction, measured over 919 days; it failed its guarded replay and stays off.
log.why: New York ran cold four days running in an east wind.

log.title: Lows read the station's own minimum
log.what: The six-hour minimum and the climate report's minimum are taken as a ceiling on the low.
log.why: Two Las Vegas lows were called at 96% on a rung the station had already ruled out.

log.title: The daily lows
log.what: Three low markets, called at 8 AM and planned the evening before.

log.title: The five-minute feed moves to the weather service
log.what: The airports' five-minute readings come from api.weather.gov.
log.why: The paid feed was reselling the same data.

log.title: The bake trail and the weekly tuner
log.what: Every bake writes down what it said and what was on offer; the per-city settings are re-chosen each Sunday under guardrails.
log.why: So timing and settings can be measured instead of typed.

log.title: Las Vegas and Austin join
log.what: The same call, record and sheet for two more cities.
log.why: Three markets a day instead of one.

log.title: The live record starts
log.what: New York's daily high is called at noon, scored against the settlement and against the market's own pick.
log.why: Everything before this date is a replay, not a call that was made.
